1.

This criminal appeal is filed under Section 374 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure by the appellant against the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 25/02/2020 passed in Present Special Session Case No. 215/2019 (Past Special Session Case No. 89/2017) by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track Court, Special Judge (POCSO Act), Durg, District Durg (C.G.), whereby the appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:-
Conviction Sentence Under Section 376 (2) of the Indian Life imprisonment (meaning thereby Penal Code 1860 the imprisonment for the rest natural life of the appellant) and fine of Rs.
 5,000/-, in default of payment of fine  to further undergo simple  imprisonment for two months.

2. Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that a report was lodged by the sister of the prosecutrix/victim on 10/01/2017 alleging therein that on the date of incident, when she returned from her school, she knocked the door of her house.

entities.text: Protection of Rigorous imprisonment for 10 years Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The doors were closed from inside the room and there was a scream coming from inside "Bachao-Bachao".
After opening the door and entering into the house, she saw that her sister was lying naked and was crying.

Further entering into the another room of the house,
she saw that the appellant was wearing his clothes.
She tried to catch the appellant, but the accused/appellant fled away from spot.

On being asked to the prosecutrix/victim, she stated that the accused/appellant, on the pretext to keep the bicycle, came inside the house and forcibly took her inside the room where he, first, opened her clothes and thereafter tried to penetrate his penis into her vagina.
Subsequently the accused/appellant being unsuccessful to penetrate vagina made penetration in her mouth.

3. After the report, the investigation was carried out; spot map (Ex.P-5) was prepared; the statement of the prosecution was recorded under Sections 161 & 164 of the Cr.P.C; the prosecutrix was subjected to medical test; and after recording her statement, the charge-sheet under Sections 376 &
377 of the IPC and Sections 5 & 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was filed.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Subsequently, the offence against the accused/appellant was registered.
4. During the course of trial, the appellant abjured his guilt and claimed to be tried.
5. In order to substantiate the allegations, the prosecution examined as many as ten witnesses in its support.
No evidence was adduced in defence.
The trial Court after completion of trial and upon appreciation of evidence available on record, convicted and sentenced the appellant as mentioned in paragraph one of this judgment.
Hence, this appeal.

6. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant would submit that he does not want to press this appeal on merits, however, he prays that considering the age of the accused and the nature of evidence which are adduced by the prosecution, the quantum of sentence may be reduced as the incident happened in the year 2017 and the appellant has remained in jail after the judgment of conviction and sentence.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the submission of the appellant and submits that the conviction and sentence imposed by the learned trial Court need not be interfered.

8. Since the submission of the appellant does not touch the merits of the case and he only argues on Sanju Kumar Singh @ Sanju Aadil vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169799076/
2 the quantum of sentence, thus, the question remains for consideration as to whether the trial Court was justified in sentencing the appellant to undergo imprisonment for life under the aforesaid sections.

sentences.text: 9. After going through the statement of the prosecutrix (PW1), it is apparent that at the time of incident, the prosecutrix was aged about 10 years.

Perusal of her statement would show that the appellant had forcibly entered into the house and after putting off her clothes, he tried to penetrate her private part and having not been successful, the penetration was made in her mouth.
Thus, the appellant has been rightly convicted under Sections 376 and 377 of the IPC and Sections 5 & 6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act.

entities.text: Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 10. In respect of rape, Section 375-a of the IPC defines that " A man is said to commit " rape", if he penetrates his penis, to any extent, into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a women or makes her to do so with him or any other person.
11. The statement of the prosecutrix/victim would show that the appellant penetrated his penis into her mouth who was minor.

The age of the prosecutrix was proved by Admission Register (Ex.P. 16)
(Dakhil Kharis Register).
According to that the date of birth of the prosecutrix was 08/04/2006 on the date of incident.
Likewise, the mark-sheet (Ex.P-14) also confirms the date of birth of the prosecutrix as 08/04/2006.
There is no reasonable defence to disbelieve the same.

Apart from that,
the statement of the prosecutrix/victim would show that the appellant/accused initially tried to commit rape and thereafter made a penetration in the mouth of the prosecutrix.
12. Statement of Dr. Vinita Dhurwe (PW9) would show that no definite opinion was given about penetration of penis in the mouth.
Considering the entirety of the case, it appears that the conviction is only based on the solitary statement of the prosecutrix/victim (PW1).

The FSL report (EXP-30)
confirms the fact that spermatozoa was found on the undergarment of the victim.
13. Section 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act suffered amendment with effect from 16/08/2019.

entities.text: Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Section 4 before amendment stood as under:
Section 4- Punishment for penetrative sexual assault "Whoever commits penetrative sexual assault shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine."

14. The Supreme Court in the matter of Vipul Rasikbhai Koli Jankher v. State of Gujara t1 considering the decisions in the matter of Dharambir v. State of Uttar Pradesh 2 and Maru Ram v.
Union of India

Union of India

sentences.text: 3 has held that in determining the quantum of sentence, the Court must bear in mind the circumstances pertaining to the offence and all other relevant circumstances including the age of the offender, and in that case sentenced the appellant therein for a term of 15 years imprisonment.
15. It appears that the appellant, at present, is aged about 27 years and he is in jail after the judgment of conviction and sentence.

Following the decisions of the Supreme Court in Vipul Sanju Kumar Singh @ Sanju Aadil vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169799076/
3

sentences.text: Rasikbhai Koli Jankher (Supra) and Santosh Prasas Alias Santosh Kumar vs. State of Bihar 4, we are of the considered opinion that 10 years jail sentence would be adequate punishment in the instant case considering the degree of offence under Sections 376 and 377 of the IPC and Sections 5 & 6 of the POCSO Act.

entities.text: Santosh Prasas Alias Santosh Kumar vs. State of Bihar 4

sentences.text: 16. Consequently, the appeal is partly allowed.

Affirming the conviction of the appellant under Sections 376 and 377 of the IPC and Sections 5 & 6 of the POCSO Act, we direct the appellant to undergo the sentence of RI for 10 2 (1979) 3 SCC 645 3 (1981) 1 SCC 107 4 (2020) 3 SCC 443 years by reducing it from the life imprisonment but the fine amount imposed by the learned trial Court shall remain intact.
17. Accordingly, the criminal appeal is allowed in part to the extent indicated above.
